St. Bartholomew the Apostle

Saints

St. Bartholomew the Apostle

Nathanael, in the traditional identification

Period
First century; mission and martyrdom details follow the ecclesiastical account
Region
Galilee, Asia Minor, Armenia
Titles / vocation
Apostle · Martyr
Commemoration
June 11

Introduction

St. Bartholomew is one of the Twelve. The OCA recounts his missions and martyrdom and associates him with Nathanael; the canonical Gospel passages and that later identification are kept distinct here.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Flayed and beheaded after crucifixion, according to the ecclesiastical life

Background

And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.

Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;

Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:

But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Matthew 10:1–8

The published life places St. Bartholomew among the apostles sent to preach and describes his continuing missionary service after Pentecost.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 1, 2

Life and notable events

The day following Jesus would go forth into Galilee, and findeth Philip, and saith unto him, Follow me.

Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.

Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.

And Nathanael said unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.

Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!

Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.

Nathanael answered and saith unto him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.

Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee under the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these.

And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · John 1:43–51

In the traditional account he labors with Philip and Philip’s sister Mariamne, survives crucifixion at Hierapolis, and continues preaching in India and Armenia.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 2, 3, 4

Death and martyrdom

The OCA describes renewed persecution: he is crucified, then flayed and beheaded after continuing to preach. These are martyrdom traditions; the New Testament does not narrate his death.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 4, 5, 6

Writings and legacy

Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day’s journey.

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.

These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Acts 1:12–14

The same life follows the later movement of his relics and the Church’s veneration. The name Nathanael is a received identification rather than an explicit equation made in John’s text.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 1, 6
